newsitem.title: JAPAN: POLL-Japan 97/98 industrial output seen up 3.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Japan 97/98 industrial output seen up 3.6 pct.

text.p: Japan's industrial output is expected to rise 3.6 percent this business year and grow 3.2 percent in fiscal 1998/99, a Reuters poll of economists showed on Thursday.
The average for this business year, derived from forecasts by 34 economists, surpassed the 2.9 percent rise predicted in the previous survey.
The survey was conducted from July 7 to July 9.
Economists said the upward revision was mainly due to a smaller-than-expected reaction to the sales tax increase in April, as exports remained robust during the April-to-June quarter.
"Exports probably outdid expectations a bit and probably so did domestic demand," said Matthew Poggi, an economist at Lehman Brothers.
Overall, economists said healthy capital spending plans, seen as a key engine of growth, should ensure continued growth in output.
Industrial output rose a revised 7.5 percent year-on year in May and the government predicted a 6.8 percent year-on-year increase in the April-to-June quarter.
